Class AutoEpochScenarioHelper

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.model.AutoEpochScenarioHelper
public final class AutoEpochScenarioHelper extends Object
Helper class providing default milestones, Tier 2 Type B engine domain validity configurations, and text formatting routines for AutoEpochScenarioGenerator.

Per AGENTS.md §8.2, §11.3, §12.4, and §13, Tier 2 Type B engines model context-dependent socio-historical, institutional, capital-dependent, or geopolitical mechanisms rather than permanent universal thermodynamic laws (Tier 1). Every engine key in calibrateTypeBEngines(String, long) corresponds strictly 1-to-1 to an executable Java class in org.ether.society.engines.tier2.theories, org.ether.society.engines.tier2.historical, or optional anthropogenic modules in org.ether.society.engines.tier1. Engines whose domain validity conditions are not satisfied by the target planetKey and year (spanning from the Plio-Pleistocene hominin horizon at \(-3\,000\,000\text{ BP}\) through the prospective horizon at \(2200\text{ CE}\)) are explicitly unchecked (false) by default.

  • Method Details

    • calibrateTypeBEngines

      public static Map<String,Boolean> calibrateTypeBEngines(String planetKey, long year)
      Calibrates the default activation state (true / false) for all 86 verified Tier 2 Type B optional engines according to their documented spatiotemporal, technological, capital, and geopolitical validity conditions (AGENTS.md §13 and docs/TYPE_B_ENGINES_VALIDITY_CONDITIONS_CATALOG.md).

      Engines whose domain validity conditions are not satisfied by the target planetKey and year (spanning from \(-3\,000\,000\text{ BP}\) to prospective futures) are explicitly unchecked (false) by default rather than masked by hidden internal sigmoids.

      Parameters:
      planetKey - canonical planet identifier (e.g. "earth", "mars", "moon")
      year - scenario start year in astronomical calendar convention (negative = BCE/BP, positive = CE)
      Returns:
      map of all 86 verified Type B engine identifiers to their default boolean activation state

    • calibrateDefaultTargetCohortSize

      public static int calibrateDefaultTargetCohortSize(String planetKey, long year, long initialHumanCount)
      Calibrates the default demographic cohort granularity (targetCohortSize) across historical epochs and extraterrestrial habitats.

      Granularity guidelines:

      • Deep Paleolithic / Prehistory (\(t invalid input: '<' -10\,000\text{ BP}\)): 30 to 50 hab/cohort.
      • Neolithic invalid input: '&' Early Bronze Age (\(-10\,000 \le t invalid input: '<' -3\,000\text{ BCE}\)): 150 hab/cohort (Dunbar standard).
      • Late Bronze invalid input: '&' Iron Age (\(-3\,000 \le t invalid input: '<' -500\text{ BCE}\)): 500 hab/cohort.
      • Classical Antiquity (\(-500\text{ BCE} \le t invalid input: '<' 500\text{ CE}\)): 1,000 hab/cohort.
      • Middle Ages invalid input: '&' Early Modern (\(500 \le t invalid input: '<' 1750\text{ CE}\)): 1,500 to 2,000 hab/cohort.
      • Industrial Revolution (\(1750 \le t invalid input: '<' 1900\text{ CE}\)): 5,000 hab/cohort.
      • 20th Century invalid input: '&' Great Acceleration (\(1900 \le t invalid input: '<' 2026\text{ CE}\)): 8,000 to 20,000 hab/cohort.
      • Modern Anthropocene invalid input: '&' Prospective Futures (\(t \ge 2026\text{ CE}\)): 25,000 to 50,000 hab/cohort.
      • Non-Earth Outposts (Moon, Mars, etc.): 10 to 250 hab/cohort for micro-outposts (\(N invalid input: '<' 100\,000\)), up to 1,000 for large planetary colonies.

      Parameters:
      planetKey - canonical planet identifier (e.g. "earth", "mars", "moon")
      year - scenario start year
      initialHumanCount - initial population (if available, ≤ 0 to ignore)
      Returns:
      recommended target cohort size in [hab/cohort]

    • initializeCulturalAffinityMatrix

      public static Map<String,Double> initializeCulturalAffinityMatrix(String planetKey, long year)
      Initializes the baseline pairwise cultural affinity matrix across all historical entities registered for the target epoch and planet.

      Affinities are computed from normalized ethnographic feature vectors: \(\text{Affinity}(e_1, e_2) = \exp(-3.5 \times \text{distanceEuclidean}(e_1, e_2)) \times 100.0\).

      Parameters:
      planetKey - canonical planet key ("earth", "mars", etc.)
      year - scenario start year
      Returns:
      map of bilateral cultural affinities keyed by both entity ID and display names in \([0.0, 100.0]\)
